html:
A South Korean film of 2019 directed by Bong Joon Ho. A poor family, the Kims, who live in a half-basement flat in Seoul, work their way one by one into jobs with the rich Park family, until a secret hidden in the Parks' house turns the comedy into violence.

The film is about class: who lives above ground and who below, and who smells of what. It won the Palme d'Or at Cannes, and in 2020 it became the first film not in English to win the Oscar for Best Picture, as well as awards for director, original screenplay and international feature, a first for Hollywood's top prize.

It was a high point of the Korean wave, the spread of South Korean pop music, television and film across the world since the late 1990s. Forty years earlier South Korea had been under military rule. Its rise to a rich democracy runs from the Gwangju Uprising to companies like Samsung.
